Support should treat missing or weak citations on scanned PDFs as an OCR/indexing issue and follow these steps:

1. **Confirm OCR handling**: Scanned PDFs require OCR; without OCR the parser extracts no text and citations cannot be generated [NL-006#NL-006-S03]. Check the upload metadata; if the file is flagged as image-only, confirm the workspace has OCR enabled [NL-006#NL-006-S03].

2. **Inspect logs and document status**: Inspect admin/OCR logs to identify the retrieved source and section, and check whether page boundaries were missed during indexing [NL-006#NL-006-S04]. Verify the source document status is not `deprecated` or `stale`, and confirm the user has permission to view the source folder [NL-006#NL-006-S04] [NL-028#NL-028-S03].

3. **Advise on scan quality and source format**: Instruct the customer to improve scan quality or re-save the document as a digital, text-searchable PDF; ideally export directly from the source system rather than scanning a printed sheet [NL-028#NL-028-S03] [NL-006#NL-006-S03].

4. **Recommend Advanced OCR for scanned-only files**: If scanned files must be used, recommend the Advanced OCR Pipeline, which uses layout-aware models to reconstruct text [NL-006#NL-006-S03].

5. **Re-index if OCR completed**: If the source is a scanned PDF, check whether OCR completed without errors; if it did, re-index the folder to refresh vector mappings [NL-028#NL-028-S03]. If page boundaries were missed, OCR logs will show this and re-uploading with higher-resolution OCR is advised [NL-006#NL-006-S04] [NL-021#NL-021-S05].
